thesis: American Express is a global payments and card-issuing franchise built around premium cardmembers, merchant acceptance, and a closed-loop network. **[Fact]** The company earns revenue from discount fees on billed business, net card fees, and interest on card loans. **[Fact]** FY2025 total revenues net of interest expense were **$72.2 billion**, up 10% versus the prior year (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260206_rpt20251231_acc0000004962_26_000080.htm`). **[Fact]** First-half 2026 revenues net of interest expense were **$38.5 billion** versus **$34.8 billion** in the prior-year period, a 10.7% increase (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-Q_20260724_rpt20260630_acc0000004962_26_000322.htm`). Stephen Squeri is Chairman and CEO.
why_market_wrong: There is no dated payoff or structural discount here. **[Inference]** FY2025 and first-half 2026 show double-digit revenue growth and record net card fees, yet the stock trades near **$352** per share where our base intrinsic value is **$413** per share but the annual return at that price is only **2.3%** per year. **[Inference]** The market may be paying for a premium franchise while embedding credit-loss and rate-cycle risk that our conservative reinvestment model already caps. Return is earnings power at price, not a mispricing signal with a known catalyst date.
